messages:
maria: Quick sync — proposal to add a "scrub flipbook" flow in Console for breakglass playback. Idea: allow a short-lived unredacted replay of request/response for support/debug, gated by quota and routing to Dedicated capacity. Need thoughts on sampling exemptions, audit trail, and routing cost/latency impact.

zach: I like the idea for debugging, but we must avoid creating a backdoor for PII. Any unredacted playback needs an approval step + mandatory audit entry. Also: if we route to Dedicated, it affects capacity planning — we'd need a hard threshold to avoid thundering.

alec: +1 on audit trail. For telemetry, we should emit a `replay.unredacted` metric and tag with `approval_method` (ui/jwt). That way Optimize can show cost regressions. Also we should rate-limit by tokens, not by requests.

julie: UX question: how does the flow look? Suggested: Console -> select trace -> "Request playback" -> modal explaining PII risk -> choose duration (1/5/15 min) -> request approval. If approved, flipbook shows with a yellow banner and a copy-prohibited watermark. Need copy of the warning text.

sam: rough config snippet for the server-side guard:

```yaml
replay_policy:
  enabled: true
  allowed_routes: ["/internal/debug", "/support/replay"]
  max_unredacted_tokens_per_hour: 50000
  approval_required: true
  approval_ttl_seconds: 900
  route_fallback: dedicated_if_available

```

zach: A couple of clarifications: - `allowed_routes` should be an allowlist per-customer, not global. - `route_fallback` needs to be more explicit: prefer Dedicated, else route to Hosted with masking and shortened sequence length. Also we should surface projected cost in the modal (estimate tokens * cost-per-token).

maria: Good call. Compliance asked for per-customer allowlist and a JIT approver role. We also need an immutable audit event that includes approver, justification, TTL, and a content-hash (not the content) for verification.

alec: For telemetry/tracing: emit these events to `audit-stream` and mark them with `sensitivity_level`. Do NOT send raw unredacted content to Sentry or analytics. If we need snapshots for QA, use ephemeral URLs that expire and are HMAC-signed.

julie: Two UX edgecases: 1) If approval is denied, show reason and offer redacted-only playback. 2) If Dedicated capacity is not available, show option to queue playback or use masked preview. Keep the approval flow < 2 clicks.

sam: Implementation notes for infra: we already have `inspect-mode` token with `inspect:read` scope. Proposal: introduce `replay:unredacted` scope that requires an `approval_id` header. Server checks `approval_id` + approval-store before emitting unredacted bytes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for `replay-guard-v1` to staging. sha: f3a9c2b.

zach: One more risk: developers might try to game the token quota by spinning tiny replays. Add cooldown per-user + per-customer. Consider aggregated token burn metric and alert if > 80% of budget.

maria: Action items: 1) Compliance: draft approval template + retention window (maria) 2) Platform: per-customer allowlist + approval-store (zach/sam) 3) Devex: modal copy + watermark + cost estimate (julie) 4) Telemetry: `replay.unredacted` metric + audit stream (alec). I'll own the RFC and will attach a mockup.

julie: :thumbsup: will prototype modal text and a compact UX for the modal this afternoon.

alec: I'll add the telemetry hooks and a proposal for HMAC ephemeral URLs.

sam: I'll spike the approval-store API and the `approval_id` header check.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone thinks this still carries unacceptable compliance risk, flag here. Otherwise I'll open RFC next week and tag legal/compliance.

zach: sounds good. tagging @legal once RFC lands. :eyes:
